lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Oh, hello again! I've been reading about <color=red>dinosaurs</color> on my walks, though I keep forgetting which one is which.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: So I've made up three <color=red>riddles</color> instead. Solve all three and three new books will arrive at the library!

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Riddle 1: I have three sharp horns on my face and a bony <color=red>frill</color> around my neck. My name even begins like the word 'tricycle'. What am I?
lines.hint: Not quite. Count the horns, and think about how 'tricycle' begins!
lines.correctText: Correct! 'Tri' means three, just like my three horns.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Riddle 2: Long ago, I was a dinosaur bone. Over millions of years I slowly turned to stone, and now <color=red>scientists</color> dig me up to learn about the past. What am I?
lines.hint: Not quite. Which one was once a bone?
lines.correctText: Yes! A fossil is a bone that has turned to stone.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Riddle 3: I was laid in a nest and kept warm. One day I cracked open, and a tiny <color=red>hatchling</color> wriggled out. What am I?
lines.hint: Not quite. What cracks open when a baby dinosaur is ready?

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Three out of three! You're far better at riddles than I am. Three new <color=red>books</color> are on their way to the library.

afterLines.speaker: Old Barnaby
afterLines.text: Did you know scientists say birds are a distant <color=red>relative</color> of the dinosaurs? I keep waving at the pigeons, just in case.
